prompt: The valve on your bike wheel rolls all the way around exactly once. In radians, one full turn is $n\pi$ radians. What is $n$?
hint: Half a turn is $\pi$ radians. A full turn is two halves.

hints.text: Half a turn is $\pi$ radians. A full turn is two halves.
A full turn is $2\pi$ radians, so $n = 2$.

explanation: Radians measure a turn by how far you walk around the rim of a circle of radius $1$.
The whole rim has length $2\pi$ (that is what circumference $= 2\pi r$ says when $r = 1$).
So one full turn is $2\pi$ radians and $n = 2$. Check with degrees: $2 \times 180 = 360^\circ$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Two half turns
steps: The valve goes from the top, down to the bottom — that is half a turn, or π radians.
Then bottom back to top — another π. Together π + π = 2π radians.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the circumference formula
steps: Rolling once means the valve travels the whole rim: circumference = 2 × π × r.
On the unit circle r = 1, so the trip is 2π. Radians ARE that arc length, so one turn = 2π.
